anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Statistics on tables and indexes are stale, incomplete, or missing, causing the optimizer to mis-estimate cardinalities and choose sub-optimal execution plans.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Obsolete row versions and dead tuples accumulate because background cleaners cannot keep pace with update/delete churn, inflating table and index bloat and adding visibility-check overhead.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Critical engine parameters (memory pools, autovacuum thresholds, checkpoint cadence, etc.) are mis-tuned for the hardware and workload, throttling maintenance workers and distorting resource usage.

When all three conditions coexist, the system exhibits severe and intertwined symptoms: execution plans are based on outdated statistics that under-represent the true size of bloated tables, leading the optimizer to choose index scans that devolve into expensive heap fetches or nested-loop joins that explode in runtime. Meanwhile, query latency rises unpredictably as each row visit incurs extra MVCC visibility checks against a swollen version store. Autovacuum or cleanup workers run almost continuously yet never reclaim space, while checkpoints and log flushes spike due to excessive undo/redo generation amplified by mis-sized memory and checkpoint parameters. Wait-event profiles show a mix of CPU spin on mischosen plans, I/O saturation from bloated table scans, and maintenance worker contention, making the performance picture noisy and hard to interpret. Statistics refresh jobs may take longer on the enlarged objects, causing even greater staleness and propagating the feedback loop.

Causal chain: Mis-tuned configuration (e.g., small maintenance work memory, conservative autovacuum cost limits, or infrequent checkpoints) slows version cleanup, letting dead tuples pile up and tables swell. The sudden growth invalidates existing statistics, but disabled or throttled auto-analyze prevents timely refresh, so the optimizer continues to rely on severely wrong cardinality estimates. Poor plans generated from those estimates further increase I/O and redo traffic, which, given the same misconfiguration, drives the background workers deeper into backlog, reinforcing both version bloat and statistics staleness. The triad thus creates a self-amplifying cycle where configuration mis-tuning magnifies MVCC debris, which distorts statistics, which in turn provokes even heavier resource pressure, culminating in pervasive and persistent performance degradation in transactional workloads.

entry.official_definition: The length of time in seconds an InnoDB transaction waits for a row lock before giving up.
entry.trigger_condition: An InnoDB transaction waits longer than innodb_lock_wait_timeout for a row lock.
entry.workload_impact: The lock wait gives up; by default only the current statement is rolled back unless innodb_rollback_on_timeout is enabled.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as an InnoDB system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
